turns.q: Tell me about yourself?
turns.answer:
I'm Jon, an independent web designer based in Bordeaux[[bordeaux]] — originally from Jersey[[jersey]], with a few years in Paris and Brighton along the way. I've been designing and building for the web for over 25 years, and I work across the whole thing: strategy, design and code, which is a bit unusual for a designer.

Outside work I'm a street photographer[[street-photo]] with a soft spot for places that have a bad reputation, a collector of photography books, and I nearly always have music on while I'm working or cooking.

turns.q: Do you like Japan?
turns.answer:
I really do — I spent a stretch there travelling and it left a deep mark on me. What got me most was the people I ended up spending time with, a collective of architects and designers in Kyoto who let me hang around their studio. The visuals, the food, the little cultural differences — endlessly inspiring.

[[next: what were you doing travelling for so long? @note:last-stop-parvati | who were the designers you stayed with in Kyoto? @note:geneto-architects-kyoto-and-tokyo | do you take photos when you travel? @photo:street-photo]]

turns.q: Do you like Japan?
turns.answer:
Loved it. I spent a stretch there after a long run through South East Asia, and after all that constant moving it was the first place I wanted to slow right down — stay put, get to know people and places properly rather than rushing between sights.

The design culture is a big part of it too: printing, letterpress, the way things are made with real care. I still think about it.

[[next: what were you doing in South East Asia? @note:last-stop-parvati | do you take photos when you travel? @photo:street-photo | which places pull you in most? @about]]

turns.q: Do you like Japan?
turns.answer:
I loved it, genuinely — I spent about three weeks there towards the end of a long trip around Asia, and it was the place I most wanted to slow down and stay put rather than keep moving. Kyoto especially got under my skin: I ended up hanging out with a collective of architects and designers there, translating dinners between broken English and worse Japanese, and it was some of the most inspiring time of the whole journey.

[[next: what were the architects in Kyoto working on? @note:geneto-architects-kyoto-and-tokyo | what took you travelling around Asia for so long? @note:last-stop-parvati | do you take photos when you travel? @photo:street-photo]]

turns.q: Tell me about the White Paper project
turns.answer:
White Paper is a long-standing client of mine — the UK's leading provider of legal and business CPD conferences. I designed and built their booking engine and on-demand platform, pulling conference data that had been scattered across disconnected systems into one place and untangling a checkout that used to take eight steps.

[[casestudies]]

The results were the fun bit — big drops in checkout abandonment and admin time. Happy to go into how I got there.
